facts.statement: The genus Liaoningopterus was named in 2003 by Wang Xiaolin and Zhou Zhonghe.
facts.quote: The genus was named in 2003 by Wang Xiaolin and Zhou Zhonghe.

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Liaoningopterus gui.
facts.quote: The type species is Liaoningopterus gui.

facts.statement: Liaoningopterus was a large pterosaur with an estimated skull length of 61 cm.
facts.quote: It was a large pterosaur with skull alone estimated at 61 cm long

facts.statement: Liaoningopterus had a symmetrical snout crest that was 12 cm long with a maximum height of 17 mm.
facts.quote: The snout crest was 12 cm long, was symmetrical in form and had a maximum height of 17 mm.

facts.statement: The fourth tooth in the upper jaw of Liaoningopterus measured 81 mm, the largest known tooth length for any pterosaur.
facts.quote: The fourth tooth in the upper jaw is with a length of 81 mm, the largest known for any pterosaur.

facts.statement: Liaoningopterus is estimated to have had a wingspan of 5 meters and a body mass of 20 kg.
facts.quote: The size is estimated at 5 m in wingspan and 20 kg in body mass.

facts.statement: Researchers described Liaoningopterus as probably a piscivore due to its long, pointed snout.
facts.quote: The authors described Liaoningopterus as being probably a piscivore, due to the long, pointed snout.

facts.statement: Wang classified Liaoningopterus as a member of the Anhangueridae family primarily due to its crests.
facts.quote: Wang classified Liaoningopterus as a member of the Anhangueridae, mainly because of the crests.

facts.statement: A 2006 cladistic analysis by Lü Junchang showed Liaoningopterus to be a basal member of the Anhangueridae.
facts.quote: In 2006 Lü Junchang published a cladistic analysis showing Liaoningopterus to be a basal member of the Anhangueridae

facts.statement: A 2008 analysis by Ji Qiang placed Liaoningopterus in a trichotomy with Anhanguera and Tropeognathus.
facts.quote: in 2008 an analysis by Ji Qiang had Liaoningopterus in a trichotomy with Anhanguera and Tropeognathus.

facts.statement: Under David Unwin's alternative terminology, Liaoningopterus is considered a member of the Ornithocheiridae.
facts.quote: Dentro de la terminología alternativa de David Unwin Liaoningopterus es un miembro de los Ornithocheiridae.

facts.statement: The parent group of Liaoningopterus is Ornithocheiroidea.
Liaoningopterus lived between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago during the Aptian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)
